subject: medicine
title: Intravenous fluid therapy: crystalloids, colloids and maintenance

steps.tx: Intravenous fluids fall into two families: **crystalloids** and **colloids**. Crystalloids are small-molecule solutions, such as normal saline, Ringer lactate and dextrose. They distribute across the extracellular and intracellular compartments, so only a minority remains within the vessels. Colloids contain larger molecules, such as **albumin**, and they stay mostly intravascular. Crystalloids remain the usual first choice for resuscitation.

points: Spread to interstitial and intracellular spaces

right.title: Colloids

steps.tx: Ringer lactate is an **isotonic crystalloid** with osmolarity about 273 mOsm/L, close to extracellular fluid. One litre contains sodium 130 mEq, chloride 109 mEq, lactate 28 mEq, potassium 4 mEq and calcium 3 mEq. Its pH is about 6.5 and it is mildly alkalising because lactate is metabolised to bicarbonate. Dextrose is only a free-water source, so it does not expand the extracellular volume.
steps.say: Ringer lactate is an isotonic crystalloid with osmolarity about 273 milliosmoles per litre, close to extracellular fluid. One litre contains sodium 130 milliequivalents, chloride 109, lactate 28, potassium 4 and calcium 3. Its pH is about 6.5 and it is mildly alkalising because lactate is metabolised to bicarbonate. Dextrose is only a free-water source, so it does not expand the extracellular volume.

steps.tx: Maximum potassium concentration depends on the **access route**. Through a central vein, potassium may be given at up to 60 mmol/L. Through a peripheral vein the ceiling is 40 mmol/L. The usual adult central-line preference is 20 mEq per 100 ml, and fluid-restricted patients may receive 20 mEq per 50 ml. Potassium must never be given as a rapid bolus because of the risk of fatal arrhythmia.

Through a peripheral vein the ceiling is 40 millimoles per litre. The usual adult central-line preference is 20 milliequivalents per 100 millilitres, and fluid-restricted patients may receive 20 milliequivalents per 50 millilitres. steps.tx: Normal saline causes **hyperchloraemic acidosis** when given in large volumes, because the excess chloride lowers bicarbonate. Balanced crystalloids such as Plasma-Lyte and Ringer lactate avoid this problem and are preferred in most adults. Recent data suggest lactated Ringer solution may reduce the systemic inflammatory response more than saline, so a balanced crystalloid is the usual choice in acute pancreatitis. Assess **fluid responsiveness** before giving more fluid.
